filename: Causally-informed Deep Learning to Improve Climate Models and Projections.pdf
title: Causally-informed Deep Learning to Improve Climate Models and Projections
parameterization_target: Subgrid convective heating and moistening tendencies, surface precipitation, and radiative fluxes
code_availability: Software is archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8239403. Fortran-Keras bridge coupled SPCAM code is available at https://gitlab.com/mspritch/spcam3.0-neural-net (causalcoupler branch, commit hash 5ebff0a6).
testbed_rationale: Uses publicly available, standard aquaplanet SPCAM benchmark data to learn subgrid atmospheric parameterization and couples back into CAM3 for multi-year online climate stability tests.
pain_points: Spurious non-physical correlations learned by standard fully connected neural networks degrade online performance, leading to double-ITCZ biases and instability.

Coupling 65 individual single-output neural networks via the Fortran-Keras Bridge is computationally expensive (~20 times slower than a single multi-output neural network, matching the cost of the original SPCAM).
Causal discovery and pruning alone do not solve the out-of-distribution generalization failure under warm climate (+4 K) conditions.
Optimization of the causal graph threshold is sensitive; suboptimal causal thresholds cause online hybrid model instabilities or severe biases.
extraction_notes: The manuscript is a submitted paper to JGR: Atmospheres with copyright 2024 listed in the supporting information. It builds directly upon the benchmark simulation and neural network setup of Rasp et al. (2018).
